prompt: NEC in ICD-10-CM means:

options.text: Not otherwise specified — the unspecified code
Newly established code — added this fiscal year
Non-essential condition — not required on claims
Not elsewhere classified — other specified

explanation: NEC/NOS conventions guide residual code selection when documentation specificity is limited or classification lacks detail. NEC is used when the documented condition is specific but no more precise code is available.

distractorExplanations.a: That is NOS: the documentation lacks detail, so the unspecified code is used; NEC means detail exists but no specific code.
distractorExplanations.b: New codes are identified in the annual code update tables; NEC is a residual-category convention, not a new-code flag.
distractorExplanations.c: NEC does not mark optional conditions; it directs the coder to the 'other specified' code when no precise code exists.

prompt: A combination code is used when:

options.text: A single code captures a condition and its manifestation
Two codes are needed to capture the etiology and its manifestation
A diagnosis is reported with a separate code for each symptom
One code is reported for multiple unrelated conditions seen that day

explanation: Guidelines instruct use of combination codes when available rather than multiple codes unnecessarily. The combination code may also capture an associated condition or complication, as directed by the classification.

distractorExplanations.b: Two codes (etiology then manifestation) is the dual-coding convention used when no combination code exists.
distractorExplanations.c: Coding each symptom separately is the opposite of a combination code, which absorbs associated symptoms or complications.
distractorExplanations.d: Combination codes join related conditions or a condition with its complication, not unrelated conditions from one visit.

0-day, 10-day, and 90-day globals depending on the procedure

explanation: Minor procedures often 0/10; major often 90—verify each code.

distractorExplanations.a: Medicare global periods are 0, 10 and 90 days; 30-day and 60-day globals are not Medicare global indicators.
distractorExplanations.b: Major procedures carry a 90-day global (plus the day before surgery), not 30 days.
distractorExplanations.c: Minor procedures have 0- or 10-day globals, and the 90-day period runs from the day after surgery, not admission.

prompt: Assistant surgeon modifiers (e.g., 80) indicate

options.text: Another surgeon assists the primary surgeon
Two surgeons perform distinct parts of one procedure
A nonphysician practitioner assists at surgery
A team of surgeons performs a complex procedure together

explanation: Documentation must support necessity; payer assistant policies vary (including PA/NP assisting modifiers). Assistance must be medically necessary and allowed by the payer.

distractorExplanations.b: Two surgeons performing distinct parts of one procedure is co-surgery, reported with modifier 62.

prompt: Add-on codes in CPT are identified by:

options.text: A bullet (●) symbol and are reported after the primary procedure
A '+' symbol and are never reported as stand-alone primary codes
A lightning bolt and are reported with modifier 51 attached
A null symbol (⊘) and are exempt from multiple procedure rules

explanation: Add-on codes are reported in addition to a primary code; modifier 51 is typically not used on add-ons.

distractorExplanations.a: The bullet (●) marks new codes in the current CPT edition; add-on codes are marked with a plus sign.
distractorExplanations.c: The lightning bolt marks vaccine codes pending FDA approval, and add-on codes are exempt from modifier 51.
distractorExplanations.d: The null symbol (⊘) marks modifier 51 exempt codes, which are primary codes, not add-on codes.

prompt: The surgical package (global surgery) typically includes:

options.text: The procedure plus any E/M visit during the global period, related or not
The procedure and related typical pre-/intra-/postoperative care
The procedure plus anesthesia provided by a separate anesthesiologist
The procedure only, with each postoperative visit billed separately

explanation: Global surgical package covers the operation and routine related care in the global period. The package covers this care for the global period.

distractorExplanations.a: Unrelated E/M visits in the global period are separately reportable with modifier 24; only related care is bundled.
distractorExplanations.c: Anesthesia by a separate anesthesiologist is billed by that provider; only local or topical anesthesia is in the package.
distractorExplanations.d: Routine related postoperative visits are included in the package and are not billed separately.

prompt: Modifier 51 is generally used to indicate

options.text: Bilateral procedures performed at the same session by the same provider
Multiple procedures performed at the same session by the same provider
Two surgeons performing distinct parts of one procedure
A procedure discontinued after anesthesia was administered

explanation: Modifier 51 reports multiple procedures; payer edits may affect its use.

distractorExplanations.a: Bilateral procedures at the same session are reported with modifier 50, not modifier 51.
distractorExplanations.c: Two surgeons performing distinct parts of one procedure is co-surgery, reported with modifier 62.
distractorExplanations.d: A discontinued procedure is reported by the physician with modifier 53, not the multiple-procedure modifier 51.

prompt: Anesthesia time for reporting typically begins when:

options.text: The surgeon makes the first incision after induction is complete
The anesthesiologist begins to prepare the patient for anesthesia
The anesthesiologist completes the preoperative assessment in holding
The patient is intubated and induction is complete

explanation: Anesthesia time starts with preparation for anesthesia induction and ends when the anesthesiologist is no longer in personal attendance. Preparation takes place in the OR or procedure area.

distractorExplanations.a: Incision comes well after anesthesia time starts; time begins when the anesthesiologist starts preparing the patient.
distractorExplanations.c: The preanesthesia evaluation is included in the base units, so it is not counted as anesthesia time.
distractorExplanations.d: Time starts with preparation for induction, before intubation, not after induction is complete.

prompt: Separate procedure designation in CPT means the service is

options.text: Reported in addition to a larger related procedure, with modifier 51 appended
Usually considered integral to a larger procedure and not separately reported
Reportable only with modifier 59 even when performed alone
An add-on code reported with the primary procedure it supports

explanation: “Separate procedure” codes are typically not unbundled from a more comprehensive related procedure. This applies when it is performed as part of that larger service.

distractorExplanations.a: When integral to the larger related procedure it is bundled; modifier 51 does not make it separately payable.
distractorExplanations.c: When performed alone it is reported without any modifier; 59/X modifiers apply only with another procedure.
distractorExplanations.d: Add-on codes carry a '+' and are always secondary; separate procedures are standalone codes bundled when integral.

prompt: Physical status modifiers (P1–P6) in anesthesia coding describe

options.text: The patient's ASA physical status classification
The anesthesia provider's level of medical direction
Qualifying circumstances such as extreme age or emergency
The base unit value assigned to the anesthesia code

explanation: Anesthesia physical status modifiers communicate ASA classification for risk/payment policies.

distractorExplanations.b: Medical direction or supervision level is shown with modifiers AA, QK, QX, QY and QZ, not P1-P6.
distractorExplanations.c: Extreme age, emergency and similar factors are reported with qualifying circumstance codes 99100-99140.
distractorExplanations.d: Base units come from the anesthesia code itself; P modifiers report the patient's ASA physical status.

prompt: Upcoding is

options.text: Reporting a higher-level service than documented/supported
Reporting a lower level than documented to avoid payer audits
Billing component codes separately instead of one bundled code
Billing for a service that the provider did not perform

explanation: Upcoding is a compliance/fraud risk; downcoding underreports services.

distractorExplanations.c: Billing components instead of the bundled code is unbundling, a different improper coding practice.
distractorExplanations.d: Billing for services not rendered is phantom billing, a separate fraud type from inflating a real service's level.

Knowingly submitting false or fraudulent claims to the government

Physician referrals to a lab the physician has a financial interest in

Protected health information use and disclosure
Technical safeguards such as encryption and access logs

explanation: Covered entities must safeguard PHI; minimum necessary and patient rights apply.

explanation: ABN shifts financial liability for expected denials when properly executed for Medicare Part B situations. The beneficiary may then be financially liable.

A taxonomy code describing the provider's type and specialty
A federal tax ID used to report the practice's income

explanation: NPIs identify providers on claims; do not confuse with taxonomy or PIN legacy systems.

prompt: Unbundling means:

options.text: Reporting a higher E/M level than the documentation supports
Reporting the comprehensive panel code when all component tests were done
Billing component codes separately when a comprehensive code includes them
Appending modifier 59 when services are distinct and documented

explanation: Unbundling to increase payment violates NCCI/CPT inclusive coding principles. Billing the components this way is contrary to CPT and NCCI rules.

distractorExplanations.a: Reporting a higher level than documented is upcoding, a different compliance violation from unbundling.
distractorExplanations.b: Using the panel code when every component test was performed is correct coding, the opposite of unbundling.
distractorExplanations.d: Modifier 59 on truly distinct, documented services is appropriate use, not unbundling.

prompt: Medical necessity means:

options.text: Services the patient requests and agrees to pay for out of pocket
Services that are covered benefits under the patient's plan
Services ordered by a physician, which makes them necessary
Services are reasonable and necessary for diagnosis/treatment

explanation: Coverage policies/LCDs/NCDs define necessity; documentation must support it. Necessity is judged against payer coverage criteria.

distractorExplanations.a: Patient willingness to pay does not establish medical necessity; the clinical need must be documented.
distractorExplanations.b: Being a covered benefit is a coverage question; a covered service can still be denied as not medically necessary.
distractorExplanations.c: A physician order alone does not make a service necessary; the documentation must support the clinical need.

Policies, training, and audits, with no anonymous reporting line
Auditing and training, with discipline left out of written standards

explanation: OIG seven-element concepts emphasize prevention and detection of fraud/abuse.

distractorExplanations.b: OIG guidance calls for ongoing internal auditing and monitoring, not audits triggered after a payer complaint.
distractorExplanations.c: Open lines of communication, including an anonymous reporting option, are one of the OIG's seven core elements.
distractorExplanations.d: Enforcing standards through well-publicized disciplinary guidelines is one of the OIG's seven core elements.

A bilateral procedure performed at the same operative session
A repeat procedure by the same physician on the same day

Disclosure of patient information without authorization

Reporting a higher-level service than supported by documentation
Billing separately for components included in a comprehensive code
Billing a service that was not performed, using a valid code

explanation: Upcoding is a compliance risk and potential fraud when unsupported. It is typically done to increase payment.

distractorExplanations.a: Reporting a lower level than documented is downcoding, which is also inaccurate but the opposite of upcoding.
distractorExplanations.c: Billing components of a comprehensive code separately is unbundling, a distinct improper coding practice.

Identify the global surgical period assigned to each procedure code

explanation: National Correct Coding Initiative edits promote correct coding and avoid unbundling.

distractorExplanations.c: Relative value units come from the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (RBRVS), not from NCCI edits.

prompt: An Advance Beneficiary Notice (ABN) is used in Medicare contexts primarily to:

options.text: Notify a beneficiary that Medicaid will cover the balance
Notify a beneficiary that Medicare may deny a service
Notify an inpatient of the right to appeal a hospital discharge
Document the patient's consent to the procedure being performed

explanation: ABNs shift potential financial liability for anticipated Medicare noncoverage when properly used. This lets the beneficiary decide whether to accept financial responsibility.

distractorExplanations.c: Inpatient discharge appeal rights are given on the Important Message from Medicare (IM), not the ABN.
